name: Westlife Foodworld Ltd
title: Westlife Foodworld Ltd - 505533 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Westlife (McDonald's India, West & South) grew revenue 12% with SSSG 4.3%, but EBITDA margin slipped on fuel/food/packaging inflation; management guides 100–150 bps annual margin gains and 60+ openings in FY27.

summary.headline: Westlife Foodworld Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12% YoY to INR 7.36 billion with SSSG of 4.3%, though operating EBITDA margin was broadly stable amid inflation.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue hit a record INR 7.36 billion, up 12% YoY, with same-store sales growth of 4.3% and positive SSSG in all three months. Growth was guest-count led, with double-digit footfall growth and the South turning SSSG-positive. Operating EBITDA rose 11% YoY to INR 946 million, but the operating EBITDA margin was broadly stable as over 200 bps of inflation (fuel, food, packaging, utilities, labour) was absorbed. Management said Q1 marks the peak of gross margin pressure and expects improvement from here, while restaurant additions were only 5 in the quarter.

financial_highlights.change: Positive in all three months; May and June mid-single-digit

segments.name: West
segments.commentary: Management described West as continuing to deliver a very strong performance, with growth aided by a rollout of the value platform and expanded store clusters in Gujarat, Pune/rest of Maharashtra and Mumbai (each ~100 restaurants).

segments.name: South
segments.commentary: South ended the quarter with positive SSSG and double-digit guest count in all three months; management cited close to 4.5% SSSG this quarter. South has more than half of the store base per management, and Bangalore has 60+ restaurants, Hyderabad 35+ and Chennai 20+.

guidance_outlook: Over 60 new restaurants in FY27, reiterated as on track; 580 to 630 restaurants by December 2027 (Vision 2027).

Management expects some cost pressures to ease as geopolitical conditions improve; targets 100-150 bps YoY improvement in pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin as an internal long-term guidance, and aspires to 100+ bps expansion in FY27 (FY26 pre-Ind AS margin cited as 7.6%).
Mid-single-digit SSSG confidence for the year, with South expected to reach mid-single-digit; management declined to give high-single-digit targets.
G&A expected at 6% to 6.5% of sales for the remaining year.
Interim dividend of INR 0.40 per equity share approved by the Board.
No price increase taken yet in FY27; annual price increase guidance is around 3%, to be taken later after consumer research.
risks_watch: Operating EBITDA margin only stable despite 11% EBITDA growth; inflation in fuel, food, packaging, utilities and labour could persist if geopolitical conditions do not ease.
Store additions of 5 in Q1 versus 60+ guided for FY27; the back-ended ramp is needed to reach 580 to 630 by December 2027.
Lower historic store economics and margin trend questioned by analysts over five to seven years; management declined to engage on the data.
Sustainability of SSSG momentum beyond Q1, and the reliance on guest-count growth while ticket growth remains weak.
Management reliance on deferred price increases (none taken yet) to protect margins.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on volume momentum and recovery in South, but cautious and non-committal on specific forward numbers (SSSG, margin path, multi-year EBITDA). Management repeatedly framed FY27 margin expansion as aspirational and avoided detailed guidance.
key_quotes: Q1 FY27 marks our strongest topline growth, highest same -store sales growth and fastest guest count growth in the recent past.
We haven't done any price increase yet.
So we are on track to deliver our guidance of 580 to 630 restaurants as per Vision 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Does current momentum give comfort to reach the FY27 topline target of INR 30 billion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said momentum is sustainable and is building on the strategy launched last year, with the first positive guest-count SSSG in October to December. It said it needs to be close to 15%-plus growth to meet Vision 2027 and believes it is on track.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margins expand with 4.5-5% SSSG, and what is the FY29 margin target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the inflation was unbudgeted and largely from fuel, packaging and marketing spend, and it is not structural. It gave 100-150 bps YoY improvement as an internal long-term guidance and declined to give a two-to-three-year target, citing levers in product mix, cost engineering, bottom-performing stores and pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Is 100-150 bps pre-Ind AS margin expansion in FY27 formal guidance or aspiration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is working towards 100 bps-plus expansion over FY26's pre-Ind AS margin of 7.6%, and that it is in Vision 2027 as an accountable goal, not formal guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 the peak of gross margin pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is the highest level of impact and margins should improve from here, with operating margin being the focus. Inflation came from fuel, food, paper and distribution, utilities (gas) and labour (minimum wages), with diesel affecting distribution.

qa_highlights.question: What is the G&A run-rate for the rest of the year?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said G&A should be in the range of 6% to 6.5% of sales, and the focus should be on the bottom line rather than individual expense lines.

qa_highlights.question: Why were only 5 restaurants opened in Q1 against 60+ guided for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was a short inventory gap because LPG restaurants were converted using electric fryers already in stock during the LPG crisis, so it is a timing issue. It remains confident of 60 openings in FY27.

capex_capacity: Restaurant network at 482 across 79 cities after 5 openings in Q1 FY27; management reiterated over 60 new restaurants in FY27 and 580 to 630 restaurants by December 2027 (Vision 2027).

Store additions were slow in Q1 because of an inventory gap: some LPG restaurants were converted using electric fryers already in inventory during the LPG crisis, which management said is a timing issue.
Last year the company opened more stores in the West and tapered openings in the South while fixing value and execution there; management said the South will see more store openings going forward.

Clusters now include about 100 restaurants each in Gujarat, Pune and rest of Maharashtra, and Mumbai; Bangalore has 60+, Hyderabad 35+ and Chennai 20+ restaurants; South has more than half the store base.
Management said the pipeline remains healthy and that it follows a prudent, profitability-led approach focused on site quality, payback period and long-term store economics.
demand_pricing: Consolidated revenue INR 7.36 billion, up 12% YoY; SSSG 4.3% with positive comps in all three months; May and June at mid-single-digit SSSG and July exit momentum carried forward.

Growth was guest-count led with double-digit footfall in all three months; on-premise sales up 12% YoY and off-premise up 11% YoY; digital contribution 74%, up about 150 bps YoY; delivery share flat to down about 1% per management.

South ended the quarter with positive SSSG and close to 4.5% SSSG for the quarter; management expects mid-single-digit SSSG for the year with growth broad-based, and declined to give region-level or high-single-digit forecasts.
No price increase taken in FY27 so far; management's usual practice is about 3% annual price increase taken gradually, after consumer research.
Ticket growth lagged footfall: management said ticket improvement started to show in Q1, after being far lower in January to March, with December 2025 cited as the inflection point.

adds.what: Over 60 new restaurants in FY27 (482 restaurants at Q1 FY27 after 5 openings; target 580-630 by Dec 2027)

growth.why: Management reiterated over 60 new restaurants in FY27 and 580-630 by Dec 2027 (482 today, only 5 opened in Q1, so openings must accelerate sharply), plus mid-single-digit SSSG for the year (Q1 SSSG 4.3%) and 100-150 bps pre-Ind AS margin improvement as a long-term goal; the store path is backed by a pipeline but no specific site or timing schedule was shown.
